svg.title: Second Shift reliability design
svg.text: Calendar: same event id per plan,
so Google returns the existing event
Every write is recorded before and after it happens, retried safely, and read back. Every risk below has a mechanism and a test.
1. Each external write is a row in the SQLite ledger
One stable key per write. Status: planned (no row yet), pending, retrying, done, failed.
A failed write stops the run. Later writes are not attempted, and the plan shows failed, never done.
Crash-resume never duplicates: the provider is asked first, so each job is booked once and each email or post is sent once.
2. Each plan has one status, stored with the plan
Only a rule-checked plan that is still fresh when the dispatcher approves can write. A simulation never writes.
Approve on a done plan returns it unchanged. Approve on a stale or rejected plan writes nothing.
What-if ("what if Wei doesn't show up?") runs the full plan and checks and replies with the impact. GET /api/whatif/scan does it for every tech.
3. Risk, what stops it, and the test that proves it
Test names are functions in evals/scenarios.py (26/26 pass, evals/REPORT.md) unless marked otherwise.
Source: second_shift/ledger.py, second_shift/engine.py (approve, _run, _perform, verify), second_shift/adapters/gmail.py, evals/scenarios.py.
The model only fills a strict schema. It has no tools.
Only crew and dispatch can trigger a re-plan.
The tech the model picks must be the sender or be named in
the message. Vague or low confidence: ask, never guess.
CP-SAT enforces the rules, then an independent checker
re-verifies. Any violation marks the plan rejected.
Sheets and Calendar are re-read at approval and the fingerprint
compared. If it changed: stale, nothing written.
Retry with backoff (0.5s, 1s, 2s), at most 3 attempts.
Writes are keyed, so a retry never duplicates.
The ledger row stays pending. Resume asks the provider first:
same Calendar event id, Slack and Gmail find_by_key.
A done plan is returned as is. Each Slack message is
handled once, even after a poller restart.
A permanent error stops the run and the plan shows failed.
Read-back checks every write on the real calendars.
Calendar is the schedule of record.
The conflict is reported, not hidden.
Customer emails are templates filled from plan data.
Gmail refuses anything but the demo inbox and its +aliases.
